author: James Allen
title: Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake maintains top spot in Suburban Council field hockey - NewsBreak
text:
By James Allen ,
2 hours ago Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake’s Quinn Stowell-Melley and Guilderland’s Tess Kachadurian battle for the ball on Wednesday Sept. 10, 2025, at Burnt-Hills Ballston Lake in Burnt Hills, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) BURNT HILLS — Even though her squad produced another victory by a considerable margin Wednesday evening, Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake veteran field hockey coach Kelly Vrooman knows her Spartans made mistakes against Guilderland.
“Today showed us we have a lot to work on,” Vrooman said after her team’s 4-1 win. “We did come out with the win, but playing Guilderland definitely is a challenge. They are a very skilled team with a very skilled coach (in Jennifer Sykes). It exposed us in certain areas we have to work on.”
Both programs competed in state title games in 2024. Guilderland ended up falling 2-1 in overtime against Mamaroneck in Class A and Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake beat Lakeland 3-0 in Class B to earn the state championship.
Although there are areas to improve, the Spartans showed their prowess on corners on Wednesday, as the team’s final three goals of the game came off those specialty plays in registering its Suburban Council victory.
“It is a good feeling (winning), but it also shows we are not perfect because they scored a goal,” Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake senior standout Addisyn Knapik said.
The Spartans (4-0 overall, 4-0 Suburban Council) allowed their first goal of the season when Brooke Lilley tied the score at 1-1 with 5:52 remaining in the opening quarter. Last year, BH-BL outscored its opposition 122-4 with 18 shutouts in claiming the program’s third state title.
The final 30 minutes saw the Spartans raise their level of play considerably at both ends of the field. Junior defender Grace Kogut scored her second goal during the third quarter and Knapik closed out the scoring on a tally with 5:26 remaining.
“We go into every game, no matter who it is, wanting to win and wanting to win by a lot. We want to dominate every game,” Knapik said. “We set goals for ourselves. We want to come out and meet our goals. We want to score a lot of goals. This one is especially special because it is a good team.”
Guilderland (2-2, 2-2) dropped a 3-0 verdict Monday against Bethlehem. The visitors were unable to generate offensive threats in the second half as BH-BL possessed the ball for the vast majority of the time.
Key moment The Spartans entered the second half leading 2-1 and completely dominated play during the third quarter. Kogut’s second goal of the game, made with 1:16 left, extended the lead to two goals.
“We talked about possession at halftime. It was probably 70-30 in the first half (in favor of the Spartans), but Guilderland got a goal out of that,” Vrooman said.
“I feel in the first half, we had more to give. We had more to give and to show we’re a great team,” Kogut said. “We just kept doing what we do.”
Star of the game Kogut is a veteran defender and one of the team’s leaders for BH-BL. On Wednesday, she showed her offensive skills are also vital, as she tallied a pair of goals during corner sequences where she began the plays with an insert and finished them camped out in front of the goal to put the ball away.
“I am just there at the end. All credit goes to my team,” Kogut said.
“We had a couple of seniors leave, so we’ve had to switch up our (corners) formation a little bit,” Knapik said. “Being able to score on our corners, drive the ball in and have great people on the post, has been really important for us this season.”
Numbers to know
13: Saves turned in by Guilderland senior goalie Leah Miller.
2: Goals tallied by Kogut. Both goals occurred when Kogut initiated play from corners.
1: Goals allowed by BH-BL through four games. The Spartans have tallied 22 goals thus far.
What’s next Guilderland: The Dutch will look to snap a two-game losing streak Friday at home vs. Niskayuna.
Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake: The Spartans play host Monday to Columbia.
